purpose: Desipramine is mainly used to treat depression. Your doctor may also prescribe it for other conditions like nerve pain, ADHD, or anxiety. It helps improve your mood, energy level, and overall sense of well-being.
how_it_works: Your brain uses natural chemicals called neurotransmitters, like norepinephrine and serotonin, to help regulate your mood. Desipramine works by preventing your brain from reabsorbing these chemicals too quickly, so they stay active longer. This helps boost your mood and emotional balance over time.
common_side_effects: Dry mouth, constipation, blurry vision, drowsiness, dizziness when standing up quickly, increased sweating, weight changes, and trouble urinating. These are often more noticeable when you first start the medication and may improve over time.
warnings: This medication carries a serious warning about an increased risk of suicidal thoughts, especially in children, teens, and young adults — contact your doctor right away if you notice any changes in mood or behavior. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms. It can affect your heart rhythm, so tell your doctor if you have any heart problems. Avoid alcohol, and be careful if you take other medications, as desipramine can interact with many drugs including MAO inhibitors, which can cause a dangerous reaction.
typical_dosing: Adults usually start with 25 to 75 mg per day, taken as one dose or split into smaller doses. Your doctor may slowly increase this up to 200 mg per day depending on how you respond. It is best to take it at the same time each day, and it may take 2 to 4 weeks before you notice the full benefit.
